extraction.output: For H4-Q1 about which ruler reunited the Ottoman realm after civil wars, I see on page 362 that "Mohammed, the youngest of the sons of Bayezid, was a man of genius: he triumphed over the last of his brothers, and united all the remnants of the Ottoman realm that remained." So Mohammed is the answer.

extraction.output: For H4-Q2 about why Manuel's support for the two Mustaphas led to war, page 363 states: "Manuel Paleologus was one of the first to feel the change in the men. He tried to make trouble for Murad, by supporting against him two claimants to the Ottoman Sultanate, each named Mustapha, one the uncle, the other the brother of the new ruler. This drew down on the empire the fate which had been delayed since 1370." So the answer is that supporting the claimants drew down the fate on the empire.
extraction.rationale: Identifiable visible answer statement agrees with the frozen acceptable variant; this does not certify a clean final answer block.

extraction.output: For H4-Q3 about what immediate development caused Murad to lift the siege, page 365 states: "At last the pretender Mustapha, whom Manuel had supplied with money to cause a revolt against his brother, began to stir up such trouble in Asia Minor, that the Sultan determined to raise the siege and march against him." So the immediate development was Mustapha causing trouble in Asia Minor.
extraction.rationale: Identifiable visible answer statement agrees with the frozen acceptable variant; this does not certify a clean final answer block.

extraction.output: For H4-Q4 about the role of the vision of the Virgin, page 365 states: "The report of a miraculous vision of the Virgin, who vouchsafed to reveal herself as the defender of the city, encouraged the Greeks to resist with a better spirit than might have been expected." So it encouraged the Greeks to resist.
extraction.rationale: Identifiable visible answer statement agrees with the frozen acceptable variant; this does not certify a clean final answer block.
